core.prompt: Let f(x)=√(x−1) and g(x)=3−x. Find the real domain of f(g(x)).
A function on R satisfies f(x)+2f(1−x)=3x for every real x. Find f(0).
Find all real x satisfying x⁴ − 3x² + 2=0.
Let f(x)=x²+1 and g(x)=2x−3 for all real x. Find f(g(2)) and g(f(2)).
For all real x,y, f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y), and f(1)=3. Find f(2), f(−1) and f(1/2).
A real-valued function on R satisfies f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y). What do the substitutions x=y=0 and y=−x tell you about f(0) and f(−x)?
For real logarithms to base b, state the restrictions on b and on the argument. State log_b(uv) for positive u,v.

branches.prompt: If f(x)=x+1 and g(x)=x², find f(g(3)) and g(f(3)).
For real x, f(x)=(x−1)/(x+1). Determine the domain of f(f(x)) and simplify it.
If f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) on R and f(1)=4, find f(3) and f(−1).
A function f:R→R satisfies f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+2xy for all real x,y, and f(1)=3. Determine f(r) for every rational r.
Find the number of real solutions of x⁴ − 3x³ + 4x² − 3x + 1=0.
